tone_statements.quote: F. LU-CH'ÜAN PHONOLOGY [Ma 1948] … Tones: 55 high level 33 mid level 11 low level 11 low stopped … Vowels: [commonly occurring vowels are circled] … All vowels may also occur laryngealized (indicated by underlining: i, u, etc.).

tone_statements.citation: Bradley, David. 1977. Proto-Loloish tones. In David Bradley (ed.), Papers in South-East Asian Linguistics No. 5 (Pacific Linguistics, Series A-49), 1-22. Canberra: Australian National University.
tone_statements.quote: Northern Loloish is represented by 'Lu-ch'üan Lolo' (Ma 1948, cited in Matisoff 1973). ... Lu Ch'üan (LC) fully voiced vs. constricted/short, glottal-stop final: 55 33 11 | 55c 22s ... In the Lu-Ch'üan language recorded in Ma (1948) and analyzed in Matisoff (1973), the hopping results in the pushing of the reflex of *HS down to 22s. In this language, the merger of the raised *2 and the high *1 is only partial; ... *2 but not *1 has a high-level reflex, 55, after voiceless initials; also, the development of *1 but not *2 to low-level, 11 after voiced ... Otherwise, *1 and *2 are merged to mid-level, 33. There is also a sandhi phenomenon, which lowers the first of two mid-level tones - ... to low-level in Lu Ch'üan.
tone_statements.locator: p.4 (sec. 2 'Loloish tones'), p.5 (tone-system table, row 'Lu Ch'üan (LC)'), pp.8-9
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Luquan Lolo (secondhand from Ma 1948): five surface tone categories split by phonation/syllable type - on fully-voiced (plain) syllables high level 55, mid level 33, low level 11; on constricted syllables 55c; on short glottal-stop-final syllables 22s; historically *1/*2 merged to 33 except 55 (< *2 after voiceless initials) and 11 (< *1 after voiced initials), *3 and *HS pushed down; tone sandhi…

tone_statements.translation: (3) Tones. High level tone 55, e.g. tɕʻi 'sheep', ni 'to tie'; upper-high level tone 44, e.g. tɕʻi 'daughter-in-law', ni 'two'; mid level tone 33, e.g. tɕʻi 'dog', ni 'also'; rising tone 24, e.g. ni 'dwell', uo (perfective); falling-rising tone 213, e.g. ni 'sit', uo 'stew'; low falling tone 21, e.g. ni 'day', tɕʻi 'nest'; short tone 32 (fn. 15), e.g. ʑi 'kernel', tɕi 'grab'. ... (15) The short tone is a very short, abrupt tone ending in a glottal stop [ʔ]; since no other tone has this, for ease of printing I omit it.

tone_statements.summary: Seven tones on native words: level 55, 44, 33, rising 24, falling-rising 213, low falling 21, and a short 32 checked by a glottal stop; Chinese loans use only 44, 33, 213, 21, 32 (no 55 or 24).

tone_statements.quote: （三）聲調 1. 高平，寫作˥（55）；例如 bγ˥ '揹' 2. 中平，寫作˧（33）；例如 bγ˧ '蟲' 3. 低平，寫作˩（11）；例如 bγ˩ '漂流' 4. 短調，寫作˨（2）；例如 bγ˨ '菩薩' 註：短調˨(2) 是很短的調子，在這個短調的後面收喉頭塞音〔ʔ〕，因爲喉頭塞音是這個調子的附屬品，所以我們就不寫他了。單字調和別的詞連讀時，往往變調，普通所見的大概否定詞 ma˩ '不' 和 t'a˩ '莫' 後面若跟有高平調˥(55)的動詞，就要降成中平調˧(33) … 還有表示擬定的口氣，往往將句中之動詞變成低升調 …
tone_statements.translation: (3) Tones. 1. High level, written ˥ (55); e.g. bγ˥ 'carry on the back'. 2. Mid level, written ˧ (33); e.g. bγ˧ 'insect'. 3. Low level, written ˩ (11); e.g. bγ˩ 'drift'. 4. Short tone, written ˨ (2); e.g. bγ˨ 'Bodhisattva'. Note: the short tone (2) is a very short tone; after it the syllable closes in a glottal stop [ʔ]; since the glottal stop is an appendage of this tone we do not write it. When citation tones are read together with other words there is often tone sandhi: the negatives ma˩ 'not' and t'a˩ 'don't', if followed by a high-level (55) verb, lower it to mid level (33) … and to express a hypothetical mood the verb of the clause is often changed to a low rising tone …
tone_statements.locator: p. 579, sec. 二 標音說明, (三) 聲調 and its 註
